First, adjacent Clutton-Brock elements are linearly combined to analytically cancel the leading O(1/r) term, yielding O(1/r³) potential decay (O(1/r⁵) density), at the cost of breaking strict biorthogonality but preserving a compact tridiagonal Gram matrix. Second, Jacobi polynomials embed the required O(1/r²) potential decay directly, retaining strict diagonal biorthogonality.
AI.result: Numerical tests show uniform-in-radius convergence for both expansions: exponential decay of truncation error when asymptotic-tail parity matches the basis, and algebraic convergence otherwise. Both bases lower the response-matrix dimension needed for prescribed accuracy.
AI.conclusion: Both new basis families are suited to studying radial perturbations in open stellar systems, providing more efficient convergence than the standard Clutton-Brock basis by construction-freeing basis elements from fictitious-mass tails.

title: Absolute Motion of the Infrared Counterpart to Sagittarius A* in the Gaia Celestial Reference Frame 3 and Limits on an Intermediate-mass Black Hole Companion
comment: 22 pages, 10 figures, Accepted to ApJ
summary: We report the first proper motion and acceleration measurements of the infrared (IR) counterpart to Sagittarius A* (Sgr A*-IR), the supermassive black hole (SMBH) at the center of our Galaxy, in the Gaia-Celestial Reference Frame (Gaia-CRF3). This reference frame realizes the International Celestial Reference System (ICRS), which is an absolute reference coordinate system defined by quasars. A combination of Gaia and Hubble Space Telescope data was used to transform Keck adaptive optics (AO) observations into Gaia-CRF3. We developed a method for selecting reference stars that minimizes astrometric transformation errors (statistical error = $0.10-0.63$ mas) and drift of the coordinate system (systematic error $\sim 0.01$ mas/yr). We find the proper motion of Sgr A*-IR in Gaia-CRF3 to be $μ_{α^{*}} = -3.093 \pm 0.085$ mas yr$^{-1}$ and $μ_δ= -5.62 \pm 0.13$ mas yr$^{-1}$ with the initial position at $t_{0} = 2016.0$ of R.A. = 266.41680848 $\pm$ 0.00000029 deg and DEC = -29.00783947 $\pm$ 0.00000050 deg, which translates to a precision of 1.05 mas in R.A. and 1.79 mas DEC. This is consistent with the astrometric measurements of the radio counterpart to Sgr A* by \citet{Xu_2022}. We also place a $2σ$ upper constraint of the acceleration of Sgr A*-IR on the sky at 0.061 mas yr$^{-2}$. This acceleration limit on Sgr A*-IR excludes any intermediate-mass black hole companion with mass $\gtrsim 4\times 10^{4}$ $M_{\odot}$ within a distance of $\sim$0.01 pc, consistent with previous studies. With the release of Gaia Data Release 4, we predict these limits will be improved by at least a factor of two.

AI.method: Keck adaptive optics (AO) near-infrared astrometric observations of Sgr A*-IR were transformed into the Gaia-CRF3 (ICRS) reference frame by combining Gaia and Hubble Space Telescope astrometry. A reference-star selection method was developed to minimize astrometric transformation errors (statistical 0.10-0.63 mas) and coordinate system drift (systematic ~0.01 mas/yr), enabling proper motion and acceleration fitting of Sgr A*-IR in the absolute frame.
AI.result: Proper motion measured in Gaia-CRF3 as μα* = -3.093 ± 0.085 mas/yr and μδ = -5.62 ± 0.13 mas/yr at t₀=2016.0 with positional precision of 1.05 mas (R.A.) and 1.79 mas (Dec). AI.conclusion: The IR counterpart of Sgr A* has been successfully tied to the absolute, quasar-based ICRS reference frame with precision matching radio astrometry, and the measured proper motion is consistent with Sgr A*'s orbital motion about the Galactic center. The acceleration constraint rules out intermediate-mass black holes above ~4×10⁴ M☉ within ~0.01 pc, and future Gaia data releases promise further improvements.

title: Fundamental differences in the X-ray accretion properties of low and high-excitation radio galaxies
comment: Submitted to Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society (MNRAS). 10 pages, 5 figures
summary: We characterise the accretion rate properties of radio-detected AGN by combining deep radio and X-ray observations of the Boötes field. We used deep international LOFAR telescope observations to identify 2840 radio-AGN across $0.3 < z \leq 2$, divided into samples that are complete in radio luminosity. We further split this sample into four different classes: radio-quiet AGN (RQ-AGN), high-excitation radio galaxies (HERGs), and low-excitation radio galaxies (LERGs) hosted by star-forming (SF-LERGs) and quiescent galaxies (Q-LERGs). Through performing X-ray stacking, we determined the average X-ray luminosities, $L_{\rm{X, 2-10\,keV}}$ and average specific X-ray luminosities, $λ_{sL_{X}}$ (X-ray luminosity scaled by the stellar mass; a proxy for the accretion rate). We studied how these X-ray properties depend on radio luminosity, stellar mass, and redshift for each of the four AGN classes. We found that the LERGs, regardless of their star-formation activity, show significantly lower $L_{\rm{X, 2-10\,keV}}$ and $λ_{sL_{X}}$ than both HERGs and RQ-AGN across all redshifts. The average X-ray luminosities for the HERGs, RQ-AGN, and SF-LERGs typically increase with redshift, which may be associated with the increased cold gas fractions at earlier times, resulting in more enhanced black hole accretion. The average X-ray luminosities show weak-to-no correlation with radio luminosity at a given redshift, suggesting that the physical processes producing the X-ray and radio emission may not be coupled on spatial and/or temporal scales.

X-ray luminosities generally increase with redshift (attributed to higher cold gas fractions at earlier epochs), while showing weak-to-no correlation with radio luminosity, suggesting decoupling between the X-ray and radio emission processes.
AI.motivation: To characterise the accretion properties of different classes of radio-detected AGN and understand how they depend on radio luminosity, stellar mass, and redshift, thereby probing the physical connection between black hole accretion and radio jet activity.
AI.method: Combined deep international LOFAR radio observations with deep X-ray data of the Boötes field. Selected 2840 radio-AGN across 0.3 < z ≤ 2, complete in radio luminosity, and classified them into RQ-AGN, HERGs, SF-LERGs, and Q-LERGs.
